items.title: Cocaine smuggler avoids prison sentence, as judge seeks to keep child out of foster care
items.summary_auto: A man who played a pivotal role in smuggling more than three kilograms of cocaine into Newfoundland has staved off a federal prison sentence, as a judge sought to keep the man's son from going into foster care.

items.title: It's costing you less to fill up your gas tank. What's behind falling pump prices?
VIA Rail heading back to Quebec’s Gaspé region after 15 years — a partial win that brings hope
items.summary_auto: Gaspé residents who have been waiting for the return of passenger train service since 2011 hope new federal investments and commitments from VIA Rail will lead to full service resumption down the line.

items.title: Skipping work to play Grand Theft Auto VI? You're not alone
items.summary_auto: Got IT problems at work? Call somebody else. Need to develop some corporate training? It'll have to wait until next week. That's because many video game fans are taking time off to play the highly-anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI that comes out Thursday. HR experts say it's far from the first cultural event to have people skipping work.

items.title: Juliet Daniel changed cancer research. Students of the late Canadian scientist say she also changed lives
items.summary_auto: Friends, students and colleagues gathered this week at McMaster University in Hamilton to celebrate Juliet Daniel, a Barbadian-Canadian professor and scientist who died April 28 at age 61. They remembered her for her accomplishments in science and for what she brought to the lives of others.

items.title: Manitoba judge stays charge in 'rare' decision after Mountie failed to disclose relationship with key witness
items.summary_auto: Drunk driving charges against a woman were stayed after an investigating RCMP officer appeared to have deliberately withheld information about his romantic relationship with a key witness, a Manitoba judge ruled.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI release means Surrey, B.C., landscaping company employees get the day off
items.summary_auto: A Surrey, B.C., landscaping company is giving its employees the day off on Thursday when the much-hyped Grand Theft Auto VI video game finally releases, in what has been billed as perhaps the biggest entertainment launch ever.

items.title: P.E.I. tasks retired N.S. justice to lead independent review into how police handled Byron Carr murder case
items.summary_auto: The Prince Edward Island government has found the person it wants to lead an independent review into how police handled the Byron Carr murder investigation, and that will be retired Nova Scotia justice Duncan Beveridge.

items.title: Judge orders Kinew government to disclose who excluded Tesla from Manitoba EV rebate program and why
items.summary_auto: A Manitoba judge has taken the "exceptional and unusual" step of ordering the NDP government to disclose who made the decision to exclude Tesla Motors Canada from the province's electric-vehicle rebate program — and explain why that decision was made.

items.title: Crimea bridge attacked again, Russian governor says
items.summary_auto: Traffic was temporarily suspended over the Crimean Bridge after ‌an attack, Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea's Russian-installed governor, said on Telegram on Thursday, adding ​that assessment of the ​damage was underway.

items.title: Alberta bill would force oil and gas companies to save money for cleanup of each new well drilled
items.summary_auto: The Alberta government has introduced legislation that would require oil and gas companies to set aside funds for the future cleanup of every new well drilled.

items.title: Anthropic's public offering exceeds every Canadian IPO combined over last 30 years
items.summary_auto: Anthropic has set a stock price of $83 US per share for its hotly anticipated initial public offering, with shares of the U.S. artificial intelligence giant set to debut on the Nasdaq exchange on Thursday.

items.title: Group claiming responsibility for Montreal Metro vandalism cites rising cost of living
items.summary_auto: A group of masked individuals vandalized the Université-de-Montréal station at around 5 a.m. Wednesday. The STM says the individuals brought in tools, damaging toll collection equipment, turnstiles and the attendant’s booth — all in less than two minutes.

items.title: Florida pastor convicted of U.S. charges in 2021 killing of Haitian president
items.summary_auto: A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted Wednesday of U.S. charges arising from the 2021 assassination of Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, a killing that plunged the Caribbean nation into deep turmoil.

items.title: First Nations health watchdog investigating how Sask. boy lost small intestine after routine surgery
items.summary_auto: Saskatchewan's First Nations Health Ombudsperson is investigating how a Regina boy lost his small intestine after a routine surgery for appendicitis.

items.title: New grad rules for Alberta high schools have people talking
items.summary_auto: Trading English for phys ed? Alberta's government says students entering high school in 2028 will only need 47 credits in core classes, down from the current 56. The government's new requirements mean that students will only need to complete one senior level course in either English or social studies, while senior level math and science classes will still be optional. What will be mandatory though is physical education.

items.title: She says Russell Brand sexually assaulted her when she was 16. She's waiving her anonymity to speak out
items.summary_auto: Mia Latter has decided to waive her legal right to anonymity and speak publicly about her teenage relationship with disgraced actor Russell Brand. She's calling for changes to the U.K.'s age-of-consent laws.

items.title: Canadian Air Force major charged with negligent performance, abuse of subordinates
items.summary_auto: Maj. Peter Headley has been charged with four military service offences related to his time as commander of Air Task Force Prestwick in the United Kingdom.

items.title: High school students across N.B. walk out over cellphone ban
items.summary_auto: Hundreds of students at New Brunswick high schools walked out Wednesday afternoon to protest against the coming broader ban on cellphones in schools.

items.title: GTA VI in the GTA? Man builds Grand Theft Auto-inspired video game set in Toronto
items.summary_auto: Ahead of one of the most anticipated video game releases of the decade, one designer has created a made-in-Toronto tribute that builds on the visual style and gameplay of Grand Theft Auto.

items.title: Gitxsan hereditary chiefs call for halt to rail cargo as diesel leaks from train derailment along river in B.C.
items.summary_auto: A second landslide and train derailment into the Skeena River in eight months has reignited calls by the Gitxsan Huwilp Government to immediately stop train hauling in the vicinity of its traditional territory.

items.title: Alberta government proposing more restrictions on upcoming data centre projects
items.summary_auto: The Alberta government is putting forward a series of restrictions on upcoming data centre projects as it sees an uptick in proposals.

items.title: Trump's team scrambles to calm U.S. fears over tech outages
items.summary_auto: After U.S. President Donald Trump brushed aside concern over the past week's series of tech outages, members of his adminstration ramped up efforts Wednesday to try to reassure the American public there truly is no reason to panic.

items.title: If Quebecor buys Telus, less competition could mean higher cellphone bills, experts say
items.summary_auto: Quebecor says its proposal to acquire one of the four main Canadian telecoms will lead to lower costs for consumers, but policy analysts and competition advocates aren't quite buying it.

items.title: Cadets being told to stand down as Canada adds billions to defence
items.summary_auto: The Canadian military has suspended most weekend cadet training and competitions in parts of the country until March, citing budget restraint. Leaked emails reveal mounting financial pressures despite billions in new defence spending.

items.title: CN freight train derailment in northwestern Ontario last year highlights risks of wheels built before 2003: TSB report
items.summary_auto: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada says a train derailment in northwestern Ontario last year highlights safety risks posed by wheels built before 2003, when manufacturing standards were updated. On Feb. 4, 2025, a CN freight train was travelling west from Fort Frances to Winnipeg when 14 loaded hopper cars carrying fertilizer derailed near Emo. Here's what was determined from the investigation.

items.title: Women's rugby players fight to save team after Bishop's University cuts varsity program
items.summary_auto: Bishop’s University in Sherbrooke, Que., has decided to cut its women’s varsity rugby team. The news comes as Canada’s women’s rugby team ranks third in the world, and university varsity teams are a pipeline to fuel the national team roster.

items.title: Competition Bureau examining marketing practices by Gap, Old Navy
items.summary_auto: The Competition Bureau is moving ahead with an investigation into whether clothing giants Gap and Old Navy are violating marketing regulations by making potentially false or misleading claims in their advertising.

items.summary_auto: The return of the Canada Strong Pass is getting mixed reviews. The pass will come back for a third year as Parks Canada is intending to lay off 517 full-time positions, and Banff National Park hit a record 4.5 million visitors.

items.title: Fiona, the hippo famous for surviving, is on 24-hour medical watch after eating a hat

items.summary_auto: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to be speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, as he brushed past skeptics and was on track to make history as the country's first Black American with the gavel.

items.title: Record-high ocean temperatures off B.C. coast attributed to El Niño
items.summary_auto: The warmer water temperatures mean lower dissolved oxygen in areas that include salmon and herring fisheries along with habitat for iconic species, like endangered southern resident killer whales, according to a scientist.

items.summary_auto: Waymo has temporarily stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways after California banned the vehicles from state freeways following recent traffic incidents.

items.title: Xi, Putin and Trump expected to meet for about an hour, Kremlin says

items.title: Biologists are using AI to track individual birds by their songs alone
items.summary_auto: A paper published this month in Nature Methods relied on sound recordings and artificial intelligence to identify individual birds based on their songs alone.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a spectacular, cynical and sometimes shallow joyride through the American psyche
items.summary_auto: Beyond an impossibly lavish presentation, the latest Grand Theft Auto game is mostly a familiar formula with some smart additions — and for the vast majority of players, it's exactly what they've been waiting for.

items.title: Why SNL's 'Sister' sketch felt too real
items.summary_auto: SNL's 'Sister' sketch went viral after it satirized the toll that caregiving for aging parents can play, particularly on women. CBC's Nick Logan breaks down the stats behind caregiving in Canada and why some viewers said the sketch hit hard.

items.title: The new milestone Voyager 1 just crossed in interstellar space
items.summary_auto: Voyager 1, already the farthest a human-made object has ever gone, has crossed the arbitrary but important threshold of a light day. It now takes 24 hours to send a message to the probe, now in interstellar space.

items.title: Deadly fungal pathogen killing frogs around the world confirmed in Manitoba: researcher
